title: Assessment of dietary protein intake pattern and perception of egg white noodle consumption among pre-aging population
abstract: This study aimed to examine protein consumption behaviors and the factors influencing protein intake among the pre-aging population, with a focus on egg white protein and the acceptance of egg white protein noodles. The study employed the Health Belief Model as a theoretical framework to explore health beliefs regarding protein consumption and its association with sarcopenia among pre-aging adults (45-59 years) in Bangkok, Thailand. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 305 participants, using questionnaires to assess protein consumption patterns. In addition, sensory perception of egg white noodles was evaluated by 60 participants, and 40 participants were included to assess their tolerance limit to consuming egg white noodles over a 14-day period, conducted between August and November 2024. The results revealed that fish, eggs, and pork were the most frequently consumed protein sources, with taste and convenience being the primary factors influencing protein selection. Additionally, 92.5% of participants reported consuming egg whites, with 79.8% using egg whites to supplement their protein intake for health reasons. In terms of health beliefs related to protein intake and sarcopenia, cooking status was a significant factor, influencing perceived susceptibility (β = -0.28, p = 0.03) and severity (β = -0.40, p = 0.005) to sarcopenia. Gender was also a significant factor affecting the perception of protein’s benefits (β = -0.17, p = 0.02), while body mass index (BMI) was associated with perceived severity (β = 0.49, p = 0.04) and self-efficacy (β = -0.45, p = 0.02). Participants rated egg white noodles positively, with an overall acceptability score of 7.02 ± 1.88 points, and reported low boredom levels throughout the 14-day consumption period. These findings suggested that egg white noodles could be an effective protein source to address the increasing protein demands of the pre-aging population. Additionally, targeted nutrition education strategies should be developed to address specific barriers and preferences in order to enhance protein intake among the pre-aging population in Thailand.
